#2845. Observations after Sixers earn strong road win over Pistons, Brown scores 30

Observations after Sixers earn strong road win over Pistons, Brown scores 30 originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers remain the Eastern Conference's sole leader.

They earned a 112-106 road win over the Pistons on Wednesday night to move to 8-1 on the season and stay at the top of the standings. Detroit fell to 6-2.

The Sixers last started 8-1 in the 2023-24 season, which was Nick Nurse's first as the team's head coach.

Jaylen Brown scored a season-high 30 points and pulled down seven rebounds.

Joel Embiid had 26 points and a season-best 15 rebounds. LeBron James posted 13 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists. Tyrese Maxey added 19 points and seven assists.

The Pistons' leading scorers were Duncan Robinson with 27 points and Cade Cunningham with 26.

The Sixers were down Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear). The Pistons' injured players included Jalen Duren (right hamstring strain) and Isaiah Joe (right hip contusion).

Nurse told reporters in Detroit he thinks "it'll be another 10 to 12 days before they kind of clear (Barlow) for getting on the court to see where he is," according to Sixers Wire's Ky Carlin.

The Sixers will visit the Cavaliers on Friday night. Here are observations on their victory over Detroit:

Embiid assisted the Sixers' first basket with a sharp pass out of a double team. He saw Brown's cut along the baseline and dished to him for a layup.

Detroit ran several double drag screen actions early, forcing Embiid to defend on the perimeter. The Pistons started 7 for 11 from the floor and took a 17-11 edge on a Robinson three-pointer.

The Sixers then made a 10-0 run and Embiid was right in the middle of it. He converted a put-back layup after a pretty high-low feed from James. Embiid hit two foul shots to give the Sixers the lead. The team raised its defensive level and Detroit's offense grew frigid.

Embiid was very good on the glass in the first half, grabbing eight rebounds. The Sixers had an excellent rebounding game as a team, limiting the Pistons to four offensive boards over 48 minutes.

Embiid didn't break out of his early-season three-point shooting slump, going 0 for 3. He's 3 for 26 (11.5 percent) on the season and hasn't made a three since the Sixers' second game.

Late in the second quarter, Embiid got into a dead-ball dust-up with Tolu Smith. After an officials' review, Embiid was assessed a technical foul for "initiating" the altercation.

Playing on his 26th birthday, Maxey missed his first four field goals and was scoreless until he hit a floater with 31.5 seconds left in the first quarter.

Brown picked up the scoring slack, tallying 10 points in the first on 4-for-6 shooting and hitting a deep, buzzer-beating three to put the Sixers up 29-21. He produced at all three levels, chose smart spots to attack and looked comfortable in the rhythm of the Sixers' offense.

Meanwhile, James did his usuall stellar work as a passer. He assisted two Adem Bona slams in the second quarter and constantly spotted open teammates. Nurse rewarded Bona's strong opening stint, playing him for a lengthy stretch.

Brown swished a corner triple to extend the Sixers' lead to 48-31. With a 3-for-5 night, Brown is at 45.7 percent from long distance so far this season. It wouldn't be surprising at all if Brown's three-point shooting improved from last season's 34.7 percent clip. With such an abundance of star power, the Sixers' hope will be that everyone gets regular open looks beyond the arc throughout the year.

As for Maxey, he sat with 3:26 left in the second quarter after being whistled for his third foul. Even with a mere two points from Maxey, the Sixers entered halftime holding a 14-point advantage.

The Pistons played better basketball to begin the third quarter.

Following a John Collins alley-oop jam, Nurse called timeout with his team's lead down to single digits. The Pistons' offense sustained some success, but the Sixers prevented a sustained run.

Embiid played an especially physical, aggressive third quarter. He tipped in his own miss and Maxey then sunk a three to make the Sixers' lead 84-68. They were up as many as 17 points in the third.

Embiid sat out the fourth quarter Monday night for the Sixers' win over the Bulls and said he was on a minutes restriction (25) because of his right foot plantar fasciitis. He played the fourth period against the Pistons and logged 33 minutes. Bona went back to the locker room early in the fourth. Nurse told reporters postgame that Bona had "neck soreness."

Detroit did not let the Sixers coast to victory.

Robinson drained a three. Cunningham made a pair of free throws and drove in for a layup that cut the Pistons' deficit to 106-102.

The Sixers halted the Pistons' run before anything disastrous was on the table. Brown blocked a Cunningham three-point try, Embiid knocked down two foul shots, and the East's No. 1 early-season team improved to 4-0 on the road.

#2843. Key takeaways from Washington Commanders loss to Rams in NFL Week 9

The Commanders entered Week 9 officially in now-or-never mode. Washington had but two wins entering Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams.

They were still in the mix despite an unreal rash of injuries to star players, due to a poor-playing NFC East.

They needed to start stacking wins, especially with a massive upcoming clash with the New York Giants next Thursday night.

That meant beating the super-talented (and also injury-plagued) Rams.

The Commanders had a shot to win at the end but came up just short in a 20-13 loss to the Rams at Northwest Stadium.

They have fallen to 2-5-1 and the New York Giants beat Philadelphia to improve to 5-2-1, putting the conversation about Washington competing for the division title to rest. Their season could essentially be over with a Thursday night loss to the Giants.

There's plenty of time to talk about that.

Let's examine some key takeaways from Sunday's clash with the Rams after watching it live:

Washington entered Sunday's fourth quarter all tied up with the Rams. That game status didn't last long. Puka Nakua – the receiver was a Commanders killer – made a leaping touchdown catch to give Los Angeles its largest lead of the day, however slim it may have been.

It was a big moment for the Commanders to respond. They weren't able to do that, coming up short on third down and then passed on a 58-yard field goal attempt for a punt.

The long ensuing Rams started working the clock against Washington as the clock dipped below six minutes. The Commanders didn't have momentum on their side. They scored 10 points in the first two drives and just three points over the next seven.

Jayden Daniels was able to work the ball into Rams territory, but then Myles Garrett struck. The Rams edge rusher — he had three sacks — flashed past rookie center Matt Gulbin for a huge sack and a 12-yard loss.

Daniels' fourth-down pass was a deep that was a short and allowed former Washington first-round pick Emmanuel Forbes to knock it away.

Washington forced a three-and-out and got the ball back with roughly a minute left. Antonio Williams' fair catch inside the 10-yard line left a long way to go. The distance was cut in half with a 41-yard gain Stefon Diggs. Washington couldn't get much farther and ended failing on that final drive.

Say what you want about the Commanders defense and its' frustrating inconsistency, but coordinator Daronte Jones' offense has been good taking the ball away. The were ranked 10 with 1.4 turnovers created per game.

They did better than that on Sunday against the Rams.

The first one came at the end of the first half, when K'Lavon Chaisson punched the ball out and Nick Cross recovered it.

Cross generated another one in the third quarter, dropping into zone coverage and then leaping to intercept Matthew Stafford's pass.

The bigger is that the Commanders score just three points off those turnovers, which kept this game tight entering the fourth quarter

The Commanders have had serious trouble starting games well. That was the case against the 49ers, where they displayed their worst first-half performance of the season. They also came out flat against the Philadelphia Eagles before picking things up, leading Quinn to highlight his team's quest to start faster and put together its' first complete game of the season.

They got off on the right foot, with Jayden Daniels owning a perfect passer rating into the second quarter while leading two scoring drives. The first was promising but ended in a field goal.

The second was highlighted by a big screen pass to Rachaad White.

Receiver Van Jefferson punched it in against his own team to put Washington ahead.

They should've had a bigger lead, honestly, especially after Chaisson popped the ball free and Cross picked it up.

A Jayden Daniels fumble (on a zone read) two plays later ended a chance to go up two scores. The Commanders gave up another field goal to close out the half (not ideal but better than a touchdown), but still lead 10-6 entering halftime.

What were your key takeaways from Sunday's Week 9 clash between the Commanders and Rams? Let us know in the comments below:

#2837. Observations after Sixers suffer blowout loss to Cavs, fall in NBA Cup

Observations after Sixers suffer blowout loss to Cavs, fall in NBA Cup originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers couldn't rekindle the magic of their comeback home-opening win over the Cavaliers.

They fell Friday night in NBA Cup action, suffering a 119-95 defeat in Cleveland. The Sixers dipped to 8-2 and the Cavs improved to 5-4.

The Sixers' top scorers were Jaylen Brown (20 points), VJ Edgecombe (19 points) and Tyrese Maxey (17).

The Cavs got 23 points from Donovan Mitchell and 22 from Evan Mobley.

The Sixers' injured players included center Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain). Cleveland was down big man Jarrett Allen (right knee contusion). Sam Merrill sat out the second half with a right elbow injury.

With Friday's loss, the Sixers are 1-1 in Eastern Conference Group B of the NBA Cup. Their next Cup game is scheduled for Nov. 25 against the Heat.

The Sixers will conclude their three-road trip Sunday afternoon against the Bulls. Here are observations on their blowout loss to Cleveland:

After a missed Merrill three-pointer, the Sixers steamed ahead on the fast break and Edgecombe opened the scoring with a slam.

The Cavs replied with a 15-0 run kickstarted by six straight Mitchell points. Much like in the Sixers' Oct. 22 win over Cleveland, they were many levels below their best in the first quarter.

The Sixers began 0 for 4 from three-point range, including two LeBron James misses. The Cavs were also the better team in transition and limited the Sixers' chances to attack in the open floor by taking excellent care of the ball in the early going. Edgecombe was called for his second foul with 7:34 left in the first quarter.

Meanwhile, Joel Embiid expressed his frustration about a couple of early no-calls. Embiid's larger problem was that he couldn't hit any sort of shot besides free throws.

He went 0 for 9 from the floor in the game. The seven-time All-Star finished with six points and seven rebounds.

Embiid has had a subpar shooting start to the year, especially from three-point territory — he's now 3 for 28 (10.7 percent) — but Friday was the kind of extreme night that's bound to happen here and there over the course of a long season.

Of course, it's notable that Embiid's been playing through right foot plantar fasciitis and the Sixers have been keeping a close eye on his minutes. We'll see how the team manages his availability moving forward and whether Embiid is able to bounce back next time out.

James didn't play anywhere near his finest game either. He had eight points on 3-for-12 shooting, eight rebounds, three assists and six turnovers.

As a team, the Sixers were 36.5 percent from the field and 25 percent beyond the arc.

Jabari Walker rejoined the Sixers' rotation as the backup center with Bona sidelined. Anfernee Simons, former Cav Dean Wade and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope all remained rotation fixtures.

With Walker and Caldwell-Pope on the court next to three starters, the Sixers cut their deficit to single digits in the second quarter. Walker threw down a fast-break dunk that cut Cleveland's lead to 48-41. He gave the Sixers some good defensive possessions when switched on to James Harden and provided his usual physical, high-effort work on the glass.

Edgecombe was fantastic in the second, sinking three triples, racking up 15 points and nabbing three steals.

Many second-year players would have a tough time finding a rhythm after encountering early foul trouble, but Edgecombe was great as soon as he checked back in and delivered a ton of valuable buckets in the Sixers' comeback push.

The Sixers pulled to within 66-63 when Maxey picked a steal and threw a pretty one-handed bounce pass to Edgecombe for a dunk.

With Embiid and James offering little as scorers, Brown hit several shots that helped the Sixers stay in the game. After his 30-point performance last time out against the Pistons, Brown reached the 20-point mark for a third consecutive game.

Still, the Sixers' offense never got rolling. The Cavs maintained their lead and extended it late in the third quarter. By early in the fourth, the Sixers trailed by over 20 points.

Embiid didn't play the fourth quarter and logged 25 minutes. He's had zero made field goals on just one other occasion in his career, back in Nov. 2019 against the Raptors.

Even with their tremendous first nine games, the Sixers knew they'd hit speed bumps throughout the year. They'll try to get back on track Sunday in Chicago.

After an outstanding first quarter, the Broncos offense lost all momentum midway through the second on a long drive that looked like it could turn into points when Nix lost a Panthers defensive back in coverage who was able to leap and intercept the pass. It was Bo Nix's first interception in 180 pass attempts.

The turnover sparked the Panthers offense who made a long march down the field — converting a third and 17 along the way — to score their first touchdown of the game and cut the lead to three with just over a minute left in the half.

Nix and the Broncos were able to respond though and picked up enough yards without any timeouts to get Wil Lutz a 48-yard field goal attempt to extend their lead to six just before halftime.

Broncos 13, Panthers 7. Full second quarter recap.

Bryce Young and the offense were incredibly hot all through the third quarter. They'd score a touchdown on their opening possession, then despite starting from their own 12-yard line marched down the field controlling most of the third quarter. On the cusp of going up by 8 points, Young had his pass tipped up and Devon Key was there to snatch it off the ground in the end zone for a critical turnover for the Broncos.

That turnover kept it a one point game heading into the fourth quarter.

Panthers 14, Broncos 13. Full third quarter recap.

Now that Denver found themselves behind in the fourth quarter, the offense woke back up. After the Devon Key interception, they would match down the field and into field goal range. A critical play on the drive cam eon third and six where Nix found Courtland Sutton outside for a chunk play to the Panthers' 20 yard line. Jonah Coleman would cap the 14-play, 80 yard drive with a nine yard touchdown run.

They'd go for two and despite having had an 80% conversion rate on two-point plays, they couldn't get it done there and remained in the lead 19-14.

After forcing a three-and-out thanks to Jonathon Cooper's first sack of the season, the Broncos got the ball back with great field position midway through the fourth quarter. With multiple third down conversions, the drama was setup with yet another third down where Nix found Pat Bryant wide open for the easy pitch and catch 26-yard touchdown to put the Broncos up 26-14.

The Panthers had no quit in this game either. They had to convert on a fourth and 18 on their next drive to keep their hopes alive with three minutes left in the game. Somehow, the Broncos defense always seems to find a way to give up a huge play in impossible down and distances. The ensuing touchdown would narrow the lead to 26-21.

On the ensuing drive, many of us on MHR staff were hoping for a second down play-action type call. Instead we got a pitch outside that Coleman bobbled and fumbled. He was able to recover, but the damage was done and the Broncos would be punting it back to Carolina with plenty of time on the clock for them to execute their own comeback.

The Panthers looked like they would mount a comeback of their own on a 21-yard completion on the first play, but on the second Nik Bonitto batted the ball out of Byrce Young's hand where Denver recovered to ice the game.

"I haven't shot as many shots as I have in my career, so trying to balance that and figure out trying to make the right basketball play. Sometimes that is shooting. Sometimes that is passing. Sometimes that is running the blitz, and it's going to help to make me better."

Mitchell tried to will the Cavs back into this game, scoring 21 in the final quarter alone. But as impressive as he was, a one-man army wasn't enough to take down a well-oiled machine like the Knicks. Especially when the rest of his co-stars struggled.

Towns's presence can completely change an offense as dynamic as New York's. Cleveland found that out again the hard way.

7 points on 2-of-9 shooting, 5 assists, 2 rebounds, 2 blocks

Watson was useful in this game. He provided some much-needed offense and was helpful as a defender. That's what you want to see from Watson in this matchup.

"Not really. In Jauary we went 2-9. I'm not really into measuring stick games). … Let's say we win by 15. Well, we might get hammered next week by whoever's in last place by 20. Does that mean we suck? No. You just take it one game at a time and try to get a little bit better."

– Knicks head coach Mike Brown before the game when asked if this was a measuring stick game

It's tempting to use this difficult stretch of games as a test for where the Cavs are. And if you were going to use it as one, they wouldn't necessarily pass.

The more concerning thing is the lack of discernible identity. When they're playing well, the Cavs can beat anyone, as we saw against Philadelphia. But what does this group hang their hat on? What does better look like for them? And are they taking steps to get there? Those are the questions that matter, and we don't have clear answers for any of them.

The Knicks outscored the Cavs 26-8 in second-chance points.

New York retrieved 41.8% of their missed shots (94th percentile). And then they made the most of those opportunities by scoring a quarter's worth of points on that alone.

"We have to rebound better collectively," head coach Kenny Atkinson said. "There's no one pointing the finger. The guys got to do it collectively. We just got to be better."

I don't necessarily think the Knicks present stylistic problems that the Cavs can't solve. An offense that hunts out mismatches with their smaller, but electric, scoring guard isn't something the Cavs should, on paper, be incapable of countering. Yet, the Cavs are consistently ending up on the wrong side of this matchup. The Knicks have their number, and there's no way around that.

Atkinson and Mitchell were asked what makes this matchup so difficult afterward. Both pointed to the offensive rebounding as an obvious issue, and one that we all can see. They also both mentioned that the Knicks just understand how to play with each other and use that to seize the openings teams give them.

"They really have solutions," Atkinson said. "I think their continuity…they just have great chemistry. They're on a string on both ends."

"They've been through stuff together as a group," Mitchell said. "They do a good job os seizing mistakes."

Brunson and Towns were tremendous once again tonight. Their shotmaking carried them in this matchup. But they also did a great job of accepting what the Cavs threw at them, and then having a plan of action for that. If you doubled Brunson, he moved the ball to the open teammate and made the Cavs' defense scramble out.

Conversely, when they threw doubles at Mitchell, the Cavs weren't quick to respond. Watson admitted afterward that he doesn't know to help Mitchell in that situation and that there are "some questions" about their strategy that he would like to ask about. That isn't the sign of a team that's on a string and understands what they need to do to be the best version of themselves.

Little things like that are why the Knicks have been better. They understand what they need to do, and the pieces fit together perfectly to make that happen. The Cavs don't have that right now. And until they do, they won't be able to get through the roadblock the Knicks have become throughout this era of Cavs basketball.

#2832. Chiefs fans boo Harrison Butker after first-half miss against Jets

Just before halftime against the New York Jets, the Kansas City Chiefs gained 19 yards over two plays and set up a 56-yard field goal for kicker Harrison Butker with seven seconds remaining. A miss to the right drew groans — but also a flag; a call on the Jets gave Butker another shot at extending the lead, this time from only 51 yards away.

When that kick went right, marking his seventh missed field goal of the season, Chiefs fans made sure their displeasure was heard with thunderous boos.

It's not just the two misses; Butker entered the game with the lowest made-field-goal percentage among qualified, active kickers (only former Los Angeles Rams kicker Harrison Mevis qualified with a lower rate). He is especially inefficient on long-range kicks; he is now 2 for 8 on kicks of 50 or more yards this season.

Arrowhead Stadium's boos represented the feelings of many in Chiefs Kingdom. The team did not trot out Butker for another field-goal attempt on Sunday, though he made all five of his point-after attempts.

Late in the game, CBS sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson pointed to the obvious: the team needs to seriously consider making the change and signing Justin Tucker to the active roster in Week 10.

She said special-teams coordinator Dave Toub was hopeful Butker would go 100% against the Jets, so a tough conversation may be coming soon between the coaches and Kansas City's long-time kicker.

#2828. Phoenix bent but never broke against the Rockets

Saturday night's victory over the Houston Rockets was easily the Phoenix Suns' best win of the season. Granted, they've only won three games through their first eight, but this one felt different. Phoenix continued its recent trend of putting together quality first quarters, something that has become increasingly important given how frequently this team has found itself playing from behind. When the Suns fall into an early deficit, players tend to press, forcing the issue offensively and abandoning the systems and schemes designed to put them in positions to succeed.

But Saturday night presented a different kind of adversity. After building a lead that reached as many as 19 points, the Suns completely unraveled in the second quarter. They managed a miserable 12 points, shot 3-of-11 from beyond the arc, and apparently decided to let amber be the color of their energy as Houston closed the half on a 22-3 run to erase the deficit entirely (that's a 311 joke). What had been a commanding Phoenix advantage was suddenly a tie game heading into the locker room.

And that's where things got interesting. Throughout the second half, we witnessed a collection of quality performances from different players on both ends of the floor. There were timely offensive contributions, defensive adjustments, and moments when individual effort helped stabilize a team that had every reason to start questioning itself. By the time the final buzzer sounded, the Suns had earned a 102-99 victory over one of the NBA's most potent offenses.

That's right. For the first time this season, Phoenix held an opponent under 100 points. And that opponent happened to be the Houston Rockets.

That accomplishment alone makes this victory impressive, but what stands out even more is how the Suns responded after their complete second-quarter meltdown. When you surrender a 19-point advantage in such a short period of time, it's easy to fold. It's easy to begin doubting yourself, questioning whether you have the personnel, discipline, or defensive capability to stop the opponent standing across from you. We've seen that uncertainty creep into this team's play far too often through the opening weeks of the season.

Saturday night, however, was the first time we truly witnessed the mental toughness and fortitude that defined this team a season ago. The Suns refused to let one disastrous quarter dictate the outcome of the game. They regrouped, stood tall, and collectively found a way to shut down a Houston offense that had been operating like a well-oiled machine. In doing so, they earned, in every sense of the word, their third victory of the season.

#2826. Panthers vs Broncos: Recap and reaction

The Carolina Panthers battled, but some bad penalties and bad luck resulted in a loss to the Denver Broncos, 26-20.

The Broncos got the ball first and immediately marched it down the field. They ran the kickoff out past the 40 then took two deep shots. Neither connected, but the second drew a rather ticky tack pass interference call. Jonah Coleman broke off a few nice runs to quickly put the Broncos in goal to go. The defense stepped up there. They stopped a first down run then got pressure on Bo Nix on second and third down to force incompletions and a fourth down field goal.

The Panthers offense did nothing outside of a first play completion to Mitchell Evans. The Broncos moved the ball quickly once again. A couple of chunk plays got them into Panthers territory. Lee Hunter had a couple of nice plays, but another pass interference extended the drive. A few plays later, Bo Nix hit Courtland Sutton on a quick slant for a touchdown.

The Panthers went three and out after a near miss to Tetairoa McMillan and a bad route by Darren Waller. After the punt, Marco Wilson got called for a taunting penalty for standing over Jaylen Waddle after an incomplete pass. The quarter ended after Bobby Brown led a group of Panthers in the backfield for a tackle for loss.

The defense got off the field on third and long to get the ball back. The offense finally moved into Denver territory with a completion to McMillan and a couple of good runs by Chuba Hubbard, the second of which drew a late hit at the end. The drive fell apart after that. Young was nearly picked by Riley Moss, then three players jumped early for a false start. They ultimately settled for a 43 yard field goal, which Ryan Fitzgerald pretty much shanked out to the right.

The Broncos moved the ball into Panthers territory, aided by a pass interference by Marco Wilson, his fourth penalty of the game. He was bailed out this time though. A couple plays later, Corey Thornton skied to undercut a receiver for an interception.

The momentum shifted a little bit from that point. Bryce Young picked up a 3rd and 15 with a deep comeback to McMillan. He found Darren Waller a few times over the middle to continue the march into Broncos territory. The offense was faced with a 4th and 1, and Chuba Hubbard broke free off the left side for a big game. A few plays later, Young found Tommy Tremble in the backfield corner of the end zone for a toe tapping touchdown.

Ryan Fitzgerald actually made the extra point this time, but he followed that by kicking the ensuing kickoff out of bounds. That gave the Broncos a short field to manage a quick two minute drill into field goal range to make it 13-7 heading into the half.

The Panthers got the ball first out of the half and carried their momentum from the end of the first half. Young found Waller out of the gate for a big gain. A nine yard run from Hubbard and a nine yard catch by Evans put the Panthers on the edge of the red zone. After a couple of ineffective plays, Young found Waller deep over the middle for a touchdown to put the Panthers up 14-13.

The defense kept the good vibes rolling. They stuffed a couple of early down runs to force the Broncos into an obvious passing situation. They got quick pressure, which forced Nix to step up into the waiting arms of Pat Jones.

Young continued to pick apart the Broncos defense with more help from Darren Waller. He also had a 15 yard scramble to help the drive along. The Panthers got inside the five. Young tried to find Tremble in the end zone, but the ball was batted away. It somehow landed on Tremble's arm on the way to the ground and was caught by a Broncos defender for the unlikeliest of interceptions. And it probably should have been a defensive pass interference as well.

The Panthers committed a couple of penalties to help the Broncos start their drive, and they were followed by a series of easy short to intermediate completions from Bo Nix. It was a 14 play drive and was capped off by Jonah Coleman running to the outside and stiff arming Corey Thornton to the ground on his way to a go ahead touchdown.

The offense couldn't muster a response. A run went nowhere, a pass was incomplete, then Monroe Freeling was blown by for a rapid sack to end the drive with haste.

The defense looked like they got off the field after a few plays, but Corey Thornton was called for a pass interference on third down, and it was another pretty soft call. A few plays later, Nix found Pat Bryant completely uncovered for an easy 26 yard touchdown.

Bryce Young led a march down the field. He connected with Chuba Hubbard on a fourth down slant for a clutch conversion to keep the drive alive. Things got bogged down from there, and the Panthers ended up in a 4th and 15 spot. Young found space, stepped up, and hit John Metchie down the field to pick up the first down. Young was hit in the head in the process, which added a few extra yards to put the Panthers inside the ten. On the next play, Young found McMillan open on a slant for a touchdown to make it a one score game.

The defense needed a quick stop. They stopped Jonah Coleman on first down. On second, Coleman dropped a pitch and the ball went bouncing back towards the goal line. Coleman eventually fell on it, but it was a loss of 18 yards. The Panthers made the tackle on third and long and forced the Broncos to punt coming out of the two minute warning.

Young hit McMillan on a slant for a 21 yard gain on the first play of the drive to move into the Broncos side of the field. There was an offsides Bronco, and penalty would have stopped the clock even if it was declined. Instead, the Panthers had to hurry to the line, and on the next play, Young was hit in the arm trying to throw the ball. He fumbled, and the Broncos recovered. They were able to pick up a first down to run out the clock.

The Panthers actually outplayed the Broncos on a play to play basis. They averaged 5.7 to the Broncos 4.8 yards per play. Penalties and mistakes were the difference. In the defense of the Panthers, some of the drive extending pass interference calls were very questionable. Also, the interception probably could have been a pass interference on Denver, and it was a complete fluke that the ball ended up in the hands of a Bronco.

It's a disappointing loss, but it was an admirable performance for such a banged up Panthers team against a 6-2 Broncos team. The Broncos are just a charmed team right now, and the Panthers couldn't overcome whatever black magic voodoo Sean Payton has done to earn his team some good fortune.

The Panthers travel to New Orleans to take on the Saints in a key divisional matchup.

#2824. Fantasy Football Injury Ramifications: J.J. McCarthy Injury Opens Door For Jameis Winston Return

J.J. McCarthy had the chance to lead the New York Giants' offense against the Philadelphia Eagles, but a hip injury saw McCarthy briefly leave the game.

The Giants may have to turn to Jameis Winston to lead the charge in the coming weeks, which boosts Winston's value just several games after being benched for McCarthy.

Just weeks after being traded from the Minnesota Vikings, J.J. McCarthy was thrust into the starting quarterback role for the Giants.

McCarthy was clearly in pain against the Eagles after taking a hard hit, and he exited the game before eventually returning.

His injury could be a future concern for the Giants, so what would a return by Jameis Winston mean for the Giants' offense?

Winston had two impressive fantasy performances for managers who picked up the second-string quarterback, coming in Weeks 4 and 5.

Aside from those performances, Winston had been underwhelming for the Giants before his eventual benching for McCarthy.

Before he was benched, Winston was able to find good connections on the field, especially with Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely.

If McCarthy were to miss time with his hip injury, Winston would need to bring back his A-game and rely on his best pass-catchers downfield.

Nabers has been the go-to guy for the Giants' offense, with both McCarthy and Winston at quarterback.

Nabers is averaging 17.2 fantasy points per game this season, with double-digit fantasy perfomances in all but two games through eight weeks of the season.

With Winston at quarterback, Nabers has had 42 receptions for 536 yards, along with two touchdowns in six games.

With McCarthy at quarterback, Nabers has had 30 receptions for 397 yards and one touchdown in three games.

Likely is having his best fantasy season this year, averaging 16.1 fantasy points over seven games.

Likely has been a TE1 this season, with four double-digit fantasy performances this season. He remains a TE1 no matter who the quarterback for the Giants is.

Likely has had 24 catches for 258 yards and four touchdowns in four career games with McCarthy at quarterback.

With Winston at quarterback, Likely has had 38 receptions for 370 yards and four touchdowns in seven games.

McCarthy has a higher fantasy ceiling for the Giants, although Winston's experience helps the veteran quarterback should he be needed.

Both Nabers and Likely remain must-start fantasy players for managers, no matter who is at quarterback for the Giants.

#2821. Instant reaction: Broncos rally in fourth quarter to defeat Panthers in another nailbiter

The Denver Broncos battled the Carolina Panthers this afternoon in their Week 9 matchup. It was a back-and-forth game between the two teams that came down to the final of quarter of play to find a winner. In the end, the Broncos came out on top registering another comeback victory to move to 7-2 on the season. Here are some instant reactions from today's game.

For the entire first half of the season struggling on offense, the Broncos had an opportunity to shine against the Panthers. Carolina entered today's matchup sporting a bottom 5 run defense, a bad third down defense, and the second-worst red zone defense in the NFL. After scoring 10 first quarter points against the Panthers, things looked up for Denver's offense.

They dominated first half time of possession and notched 15 first downs and 159 yards of total offense. Unfortunately, a Bo Nix interception in enemy territory proved to be a big momentum change in the game. In addition to that, Denver's interior offensive line was manhandled in the first two quarters. Ben Powers and Luke Wattenberg struggled with Lee Hunter and Derrick Brown and Denver gained just 34 yards on the ground in the first half.

The Broncos' offense wasn't on the field much in the third quarter. But as usual, four quarter heroics once again came into focus. Denver was able to carve out two scoring drives. The first was a 17-play drive that went 80 yards and was capped off with a Jonah Coleman touchdown run. On their next possession, Nix was able to hit Pat Bryant on a beautiful 26-yard touchdown throw.

The touchdowns were great, but it was awesome to see Nix and the offense perform well on third down. They had a lot of big drive-sustaining conversions that made the final touchdowns possible. But that pitch to Coleman late in the game that could have cost Denver the win? Oof. That certainly raised the collective blood pressure of Broncos Country.

I was hoping for more effectiveness in the ground game, but I'm happy to see Denver's offense come together in the fourth quarter and ignite to lead the Broncos to victory. Their success was a big part of why they were able to get their fifth-straight victory of the season. Well done, offense!

The Broncos entered today's matchup with several key starters out on defense. The starting safety tandem of Brandon Jones and Talanoa Hufanga were out, making Devon Key and J.L. Skinner the next men up. Defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike was also inactive after being placed on injured reserve.

To make things worse, Riley Moss exited the game in the second quarter after suffering a concussion. Down four starters, Bryce Young and the Panthers' offense was able to gain some steam and have success. Carolina reeled off back-to-back touchdown drives at the end of the first half and the start of the second half to take a 14 to 13 lead in the third quarter.

Whether it was the pass or the run, Vance Joseph's defense couldn't find a way to get them off the field. Young had an impressive streak of fifteen-straight completed passes. A big issue all game long was the absence of a formidable pass rush which was quite a bit of a surprise.

The Panthers entered today's matchup allowing 23 sacks. Denver wasn't able to take down Young until halfway through the four quarter when Jonathon Cooper came up big on third down and finally brought the fourth-year signal caller down.

The defense had two big plays that saved their poor play throughout the contest. The first was when Key was able to intercept a pass in the endzone that bounced off Tommy Tremble's right arm. To end the game, Nik Bonitto was able to strip sack Young in the final minutes of play to seal the deal for the Broncos.

I'll say this though, Denver giving up so many third-and-long plays, even with the injuries, was extremely concerning. I thought Joseph's conservative playcalling late in the game was perplexing. The defense will have a lot of reflection to do over the bye week to rectify some of the issues we have seen recently, but I'm happy they were able to close the game out with a big turnover.

What a ride Jeremy Sochan has had, and the new season is just getting underway. After nearly four seasons with the San Antonio Spurs, he was waived and signed with the Knicks, picking up a championship ring when New York beat the Spurs in the 2026 Finals.

#2817. Winners and losers from Georgia football's 42-7 win at Ole Miss

The Georgia Bulldogs faced the Mississippi Rebels on the road in another highly anticipated SEC contest on Saturday. The Rebels had a 16-game home win streak, but the Bulldogs halted it, winning 42-7 to raise their record to 8-1 this season, while Mississippi is 6-3. Here are the winners and losers from the game.

Georgia's offense was electric during the game, scoring 42 total points. Quarterback Gunner Stockton went 9 for 15 for 186 yards and four touchdown passes. Wide receiver Talyn Taylor had a great performance, catching four passes for 140 yards and three touchdowns. Running back Nate Frazier looked great, leading the team in rushing with 107 yards on 16 carries.

Mississippi wide receiver Horatio Fields was one of the only bright spots for them on offense, catching eight passes for 96 yards. Fields led the team in receiving and was a reliable target for Trinidad Chambliss.

Georgia's defense looked fantastic against Ole Miss. The Bulldogs dominated the Ole Miss offensive front and shut down the Rebels until garbage time in the fourth quarter. Georgia sacked Ole Miss five times and forced a pair of Ole Miss turnovers.

Georgia kicker Peyton Woodring missed his lone field goal in the matchup. He missed a 49-yard field goal before halftime. This is the fourth consecutive game where he's missed. But he did make all of his point after attempts. Woodring has made nine of 13 kicks this season.

Mississippi's offense did not have a good game, scoring only seven points. Trinidad Chambliss was sacked five times. They weren't able to get much going. Chambliss was forced out of the pocket multiple times and threw an interception to Georgia safety K.J. Bolden. The Rebels' run game was nonexistent, rushing for 66 yards. The Ole Miss offensive line has a very poor day and could not defend Georgia's blitz.

Georgia will take on Missouri on Saturday, November 14th.

#2812. Against Oklahoma City, the Wizards were the bug

Oklahoma City Thunder broadcaster Michael Cage summed up this game perfectly: "In this game, sometimes you're the bug, and sometimes you're the windshield." In this one, the Wizards were in the role of the bug.

Washington was no match for the Thunder. Oklahoma City took control early and the Wizards had no answer for their athleticism, execution, and swarming defensive presence.

The Wizards converted just 29.6% of their field goal attempts, including 7-43 from three-point range. That's 16.3%. Which is bad. Very bad.

Positives for the Wizards were scarce. Among them — Alex Sarr grabbed 14 rebounds in 28 minutes. Bub Carrington shot 3-3 from deep. Bilal Coulibaly defended Shai Gilgeous-Alexander pretty well in the first quarter — SGA had two points on o-3 shooting when Coulibaly left the game. He immediately started scoring and finished the game with 30 points and 9 assists.

For Washington, it's a third consecutive loss — their first three-game skid of the season. Before the game, head coach Brian Keefe talked with reporters about the team figuring out their formula for success. The team would be wise not to over-index on this game. It was a bad result, and the team looked awful.

Despite missing Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren (in some order, their second and third best players), OKC is a special case. It's a championship-level team with something to prove. The Wizards need to learn to compete at that level, and the lesson of their last three games is that they're still not close.

That's not the end of world 10 games into the season. But they need to internalize that lesson and do the work to become competitive against high-level opponents.

Kudos to the OKC stadium operations team — when the Wizards starters got introduced, they played Harry Potter theme music. Good job.

The Wizards entered the game with the NBA's second best "in the paint" field goal percentage (62.2%). The Thunder had the NBA's second best defensive paint FG% (holding opponents to just 50.2%). Safe to say OKC won that battle.

In the first quarter, the Wizards ran a pick-and-roll option out of a horns set for AJ Dybantsa. He had a choice of going left or right. It didn't go great — he ended up battling his way into a mid-ranger, which he missed. The set was good, though.

Tre Mann got real minutes for the first time this season. He looked pretty good — quick, aggressive, athletic. I'd like to see more.

Jotted during the second quarter (could have been jotted anytime) — OKC defenders switch HARD.

Another second quarter note — OKC was doubling Trae Young to get the ball out of his hands. The other Wizards weren't able to take make plays, in part because OKC defenders hustled back to their matchups and rotated so perfectly.

I thought maybe the Wizards had a chance of making things respectable — a thought that disappeared when I saw their possession of the second half. It was a pick-and-roll for Kyshawn George, who got caught in no-man's land. The only teammate who cut was Coulibaly, who didn't get free. That should have triggered a cascade of movement, but the other guys stood around until George was forced to take a difficult shot, which he missed.

The Wizards tried a small-ball lineup in the second half. It got shredded by Aday Mara and the Thunder.

#2809. Broncos DB Devon Key awarded wild interception in the Panthers' end zone after Denver challenge

In Sunday's matchup between the Carolina Panthers and Denver Broncos, a dropped touchdown pass turned into an unbelievable interception thanks to a well-timed challenge, a key play in Denver's tight road victory.

Toward the end of the third quarter, Panthers quarterback Bryce Young threw a pass to tight end Tommy Tremble in the end zone. Though the ball ended up in the hands of Broncos defensive back Devon Key, it looked like it hit the ground first, leading officials to rule the play incomplete.

Denver used its challenge flag, leading to a review that proved successful for the Broncos. As Tremble went down while trying to make the catch, the ball rolled off his wrist before bouncing off his hand, with Key in just the right position to pluck it out of the air. It never actually hit the ground, leading officials to overturn the call and rule it a Denver pick.

Devon Key somehow got the interception in the Panthers end zone.

Because the play was ruled dead, Key did not get a chance to make a return, but the Broncos were given a touchback. Quarterback Bo Nix then led the team down the field on a 14-play, 80-yard touchdown drive to take a 19-15 lead, after Denver's 2-point conversion attempt was unsuccessful.

The game stayed tight until the end. Though the Broncos scored another fourth-quarter touchdown shortly afterward, the Panthers came back with Young finding Tetairoa McMillan in the end zone on the next drive.

A three-and-out Denver drive gave Carolina a late chance for a go-ahead touchdown, but Nik Bonitto forced Young's second turnover of Sunday with a sack and fumble recovery. The Broncos (7-2) then rode out the final minute and change for a 26-21 win.

No problem, because there was no doubt about his second sack of the game in the fourth quarter, beating the left tackle and getting to Daniels in the pocket. Kyren Williams is still the starter, but Corum has become the Rams' bigger playmaker out of the backfield and finished with a team-high 58 yards on 11 carries.

Landman punched out the ball twice in this game, though neither resulted in a recovered fumble by the Rams. New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy briefly left Sunday's 19-11 win over the Philadelphia Eagles early with an apparent hip injury after he took a direct shot to his side.

McCarthy, however, returned two drives later at Lincoln Financial Field and appeared to avoid any major injury.

#2804. Jaxon Smith-Njigba can do something no one has done since 1960

Maybe this year they’ll send Jaxon Smith-Njigba a trophy without a typo.

The Seahawks receiver, through eight games, remains on pace to become the first player to generate more than 2,000 receiving yards in a single season.

His 985 yards project to 2,093 yards for the full season.

The current record is held by Hall of Famer Calvin Johnson, who gained 1,964 yards in 2012 with the Lions.

And for those who would argue that an asterisk should apply based on the extension of the season to 17 games, Smith-Njigba’s current production puts him on pace for 1,970 yards in 16 games.

There’s something more immediate that Smith-Njigba can achieve. With 115 receiving yards and a touchdown against the Cardinals on Sunday, Smith-Njigba will become only the fourth player in NFL history with 1,100 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns through the first nine games of a season.

The others were Hall of Famer Don Hutson in 1942, Hall of Famer Elroy “Crazy Legs” Hirsch in 1951, and Hall of Famer Raymond Berry in 1960.

It’s amazing that it hasn’t happened in 66 years. With the rules that loosened the passing game in the 1970s, and given the many great receivers who have played over the past six decades (Jerry Rice, Randy Moss, Terrell Owens, just to name three), no one has done what Smith-Njigba could do today.

#2801. Commanders vs. Rams Week 9 Player of the Game: LB Frankie Luvu

The Washington Commanders came out swinging against the Los Angeles Rams today, but ultimately fell, bringing their record to 2-5-1.

After taking a 10-6 lead into the locker room at halftime, the Commanders struggled to get the offense going. Suddenly, they struggled to sustain drives, penalties became a problem, and the defense spent too much time on the field. They managed a field goal in the third quarter, but the Rams scored 14 points to win the game 20-13.

Despite the defense spending so much time on the field today, veteran linebacker Frankie Luvu understood the assignment. He stepped up in a big way to support a depleted defensive line, and he set the tone for the game, earning Player of the Game honors.

Luvu led the game with 15 tackles (seven solo), one sack, two tackles for loss, and two quarterback hits. He was everywhere he needed to be on the field Sunday, and he is showing the rest of the defense what they should be doing, too. Before this season started, Luvu said that he was focused on putting last year behind him and being a leader on this team.

Today, Luvu stood out as a defensive leader. Knowing how many injuries are plaguing the defensive line, he knew that the linebackers would have to step up. And that's exactly what he did. Sonny Styles and Nick Cross were terrific, too, but Luvu is our Week 9 Player of the Game.

#2796. Steelers Alum Jack Ham in Stable Condition After Experiencing Medical Emergency Ahead of Penn State Game Broadcast

Pittsburgh Steelers alum Jack Ham, 77, experienced a medical emergency while he was preparing for Penn State's game broadcast in Seattle on Nov. 7

"It was a gut-wrenching day for Penn State football, with Jack Ham," Nittany Lions coach Matt Campbell said

Ham's broadcast partner, Steve Jones, made a "heroic effort" to assist Ham, and the NFL star was taken to the University of Washington Medical Center

Pittsburgh Steelers great Jack Ham is in stable condition after experiencing a medical emergency while he was preparing for Penn State's game broadcast over the weekend — and the college team is crediting Ham's co-host for helping him make it to the hospital.

After Penn State's 28-25 victory over the University of Washington in Seattle on Saturday, Nov. 7, Nittany Lions coach Matt Campbell revealed that Ham, 77, experienced a medical emergency as he was arriving at Husky Stadium.

Ham's broadcast partner, Steve Jones, then made a "heroic effort" to assist Ham, per ESPN and the Associated Press.

"It was a gut-wrenching day for Penn State football, with Jack Ham. Obviously a really tough situation as we got off the buses here," Campbell said. "Steve Jones and the heroic effort that he did for someone he loves dearly. If not for Steve and what he did, I don't know if we would have as good news as we have right now."

Jack Ham during a game against the Los Angeles Rams at Three Rivers Stadium in Pittsburgh, Pa., on Nov. 29, 1981Credit: George Gojkovich/Getty

"I would also thank the University of Washington, their athletic director, their emergency team," the head coach added, referring to Washington athletic director Patrick Chun and the Huskies' staff. "They were incredible, they were outstanding."

Ham was quickly taken across the street to the University of Washington Medical Center after the emergency, Penn State Athletics told PEOPLE in a statement.

"Penn State Sports Network analyst Jack Ham experienced a medical emergency earlier today and was transported to the University of Washington Medical Center, where he is being treated," an athletics spokesperson wrote. "We do not have further information at this time."

Originally from Johnstown, Pa., Ham has been the radio analyst for Penn State, his alma mater, since 2000. The former linebacker was a six-time All-Pro selection with the Steelers and went on to win four Super Bowls and play in eight Pro Bowl games.

Never miss a story — sign up for PEOPLE's free daily newsletter to stay up-to-date on the best of what PEOPLE has to offer, from celebrity news to compelling human interest stories.

He entered the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1988 and the College Football Hall of Fame in 1990, and was named to the NFL's 1970s All-Decade Team.

Campbell shared during Saturday's press conference that he told the Penn State players about Ham's status before kickoff.

"The courage of our kids to play with what Jack Ham means to Penn State football, how that guy played the game, how that guy to this day still serves our football program, it was awesome to be able to go win the football game for him and his family," Campbell said, per AP. "Our thoughts and prayers will continue to be with him for a full recovery."

#2794. Eagles-Giants final score: Philadelphia loses at home to New York for first time since 2013

The Philadelphia Eagles are 2-7 after losing to the New York Giants on Sunday afternoon. Final score: 19 to 11.

This marks the Eagles' seventh straight loss. The Birds are 5-12 in their last 17 games, which is the equivalent of a full regular season.

This result also marks the Eagles' first loss to the Giants in Philly since the 2013 season. A historic loss in a historically bad season.

The Eagles turned to Joe Milton at quarterback for a spark but they did not get it. The offense was pretty ineffective all day long. Vic Fangio's defense mostly battled … but their effort wasn't enough.

Next up for the Eagles: the NFL trade deadline is at 4:00 PM Eastern on Tuesday, November 10 before the Eagles' bye in Week 10. They'll return to host the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 11.

Read on for a recap and stay tuned for BGN's postgame coverage. Also, check me out talking about this game on the PHLY Eagles postgame show.

The Eagles won the coin toss and elected to defer, per usual. The Giants took over at their own 20-yard line after Jake Elliott's kickoff bounced in the landing zone into the end zone. Not sarcasm: good start! Facing 3rd-and-5 after Zack Baun exploded into the backfield for a TFL, J.J. McCarthy faced zero pressure and hit a wide open Isaiah Likely for an easy first down. Facing 3rd-and-12 after Jordan Davis got to Devin Singletary for a TFL, McCarthy had another clean pocket to find a wide open Darnell Mooney for another first down. Eagles defense making it look easy for the Giants' offense. Facing 3rd-and-10 after Riq Woolen tipped a pass incomplete, Vic Fangio brought a blitz and Baun got to McCarthy for a sack. Nice! The Giants brought in Dominic Zvada for a 53-yard field goal make. EAGLES 0, GIANTS 3.

The Eagles took over at their own 17-yard line after just a 12-yard kick return by Jaydon Blue. Joe Milton was flagged for a false start to begin the game. Great stuff! Detailed. Facing 3rd-and-7 after Milton's first Eagles passing attempt was caught by Dallas Goedert, Milton threw behind Darius Cooper to bring up three-and-out. The broadcast said Cooper should've sat down on his route since he was open. But there's naturally going to be some miscommunication with Milton and his receivers after barely getting a chance to work with them.

The Giants took over at their own 46-yard line after Kelee Ringo got called for unsportsmanlike conduct for running out of bounds on punt coverage and not making a good enough effort to get back in the field of play. Facing 3rd-and-5 after two runs, McCarthy hit Malik Nabers with Kenny Moore II trailing. Andrew Mukuba got away with a helmet-to-helmet on the play. It was originally ruled Marcus Epps forced a fumble after a Likely catch for an Eagles recovery … but replay easily revealed it was a Giants catch. Facing 3rd-and-4, McCarthy held the ball and ran backwards into a waiting Jonathan Greenard for a sack. Well, it wasn't exactly a great rush, but Greenard is on the board. The Giants settled for a 49-yard field goal make. EAGLES 0, GIANTS 6.

The Eagles took over at their own 42-yard line after the Giants had an unnecessary roughness penalty on kickoff coverage. Milton was sacked with Kayvon Thibodeaux absolutely cooking Markel Bell to set up D.J. Reader for a sack. Facing 3rd-and-6, the Giants brought extra defenders but Milton was able to take off running for 19 yards and a first down into Giants territory. Facing 3rd-and-9, Milton aired it out down the right sideline and Darius Cooper drew a 30-yard defensive pass interference penalty! Weirdly underthrown ball led to the penalty, but, hey, the Eagles will take it. Facing 3rd-and-goal from the 3-yard line, Saquon Barkley took a carry to the end zone! Jake Elliott made his extra point attempt but the Giants were flagged for 12 men on the field to allow the Eagles a two-point try from the one-yard line. Milton took the tush push to the end zone for two and then celebrated with a backflip in the end zone! Nice job by Nick Sirianni to maximize points there. And nice job by the offense (a rare thing) on an 8-play, 58-yard TD drive! EAGLES 8, GIANTS 6.

The Giants took over at their own 20-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-2, Zack Baun helped to stuff a Giants run to force a three-and-out! Is this team actually playing good football for once?

The Eagles took over at their own six-yard line after Riq Woolen committed a special teams penalty.

Facing 3rd-and-2 after two Barkley runs, Milton sailed a pass to a tightly covered Makai Lemon on a crossing pattern. The Eagles went three-and-out … but the Giants muffed the punt and Eagles rookie long snapper Rocco Underwood recovered the ball! Facing 3rd-and-5, Milton got LIT UP by unblocked Giants rookie Arvell Reese and New York recovered the fumble. Not sure who that pass protection breakdown was on? Milton for not seeing the blitz? The offensive line? Mitchell for picking up no one? All of the above? Regardless, it's yet another example of the Eagles being unable to deal with unblocked pressure. No NFL team is worse in that category.

The Giants took over at the 50-yard line and instantly got knocked back by a holding penalty. Facing 3rd-and-13 after Carter strip-sacked McCarthy but the Giants recovered the ball, McCarthy's checkdown brought up another three-and-out forced by Vic Fangio's defense.

The Eagles took over at their own 11-yard line. Milton to Lemon in the slot resulted in a first down, nice strike. Milton found Lemon again for another first down. Facing 3rd-and-10 after Lemon dropped a pass that would've at least set up a more manageable third down, Milton was blitzed and sacked. Braden Mann's punt was shanked for just 17 yards, though the Giants got called for holding to make it a 27-yard net for the Eagles. When it rains, it pours.

The Giants took over at their own 29-yard line. They picked up a first down with Jordan Davis getting flagged for roughing the passer (his hands touched McCarthy's helmet). Jalyx Hunt picked up a TFL (his second of the season and first since Week 2) on a Giants trick play attempt. Then Baun got to McCarthy on a blitz. Facing 3rd-and-22, the Giants went with a bubble screen to pick up some yards before a punt.

The Eagles took over at their own 18-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-1, Barkley picked up a first down on the ground. The Eagles had to burn their first timeout with the play clock winding down. Milton ripped a 20-yard completion to Cooper to move the Eagles into plus territory. Facing 3rd-and-7, Milton to Cooper over the middle picked up six yards. Facing 4th-and-1, the Eagles lined up in shotgun to pretend to snap the ball before the clock hit 2:00. Why not line up for the tush push there? More believable the Eagles might actually go for it from that formation. Facing 4th-and-1 for real, the Eagles lined up in the gun again … and a handoff to Barkley for stuffed for a turnover on downs. Why not the tush push there? Or at least line up in that formation.

The Giants took over at their own 41-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-14, McCarthy ran out of bounds to bring up a punt and fourth straight three-and-out forced.

The Eagles took over at their own 2-yard line with 0:34 on the clock and two timeouts to work with. Facing 3rd-and-8 after two runs to force the Giants to burn two timeouts, another Barkley run forced the Giants to take their final timeout. Mann booted the ball over the Giants' returners' head for an 86-yard punt! That was awesome. And a funny way to follow up Mann's previous punt, a 17-yarder.

The Giants took a knee to end the first half.

The Eagles took over at their own 27-yard line. A Drew Kendall holding penalty wiped out a Milton nine-yard run and knocked the offense back. Facing 3rd-and-24 after Kendall was driven back into Milton to create a Giants sack, Milton dodged pressure and took off running to bring up a punt. Mann booted the ball a mere 60 yards this time.

The Giants took over at their own 15-yard line. Singletary dodged a Quinyon Mitchell whiff en route to a first down on the ground. Three-and-out streak over. McCarthy took off running and got hurt after lowering his shoulder and taking a big hit. Dumb stuff from the Giants' QB. Jameis Winston entered the game at quarterback. Facing 3rd-and-8, Winston had Nabers for a first down but the throw went wide. Meanwhile, the broadcast showed McCarthy in serious pain after trying to throw the ball while on the sideline.

The Eagles took over at their own 22-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-10 after two Milton incompletions, DC failed to make what would've been an impressive leaping catch while being tackled. Three-and-out.

The Giants took over at their own 24-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-16 after Nolan Smith picked up his fifth sack of the season, Winston hit Malachi Fields at the marker (with Cooper DeJean and Riq Woolen leaving a soft spot in coverage) for a big first down conversion. Facing 3rd-and-8, Singletary spun out of bounds with the ball just shy of the marker. Facing 4th-and-1, the Giants went tush push for a first down. Winston ran for a first down on a broken play where the Eagles missed five tackles. Winston then hit Mooney for 27 yards to put the Giants in the red zone for the first time in this game. Then Winston hit Fields to bring up 1st-and-goal from the 2-yard line. Then Winston hit a WIDE open Likely for a go-ahead touchdown. 14-play, 76-yard TD drive that took 7:56 off the clock. EAGLES 8, GIANTS 13.

The Eagles took over at their own 21-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-13 after two runs, Milton checked down to Mitchell to bring up a punt.

The Giants took over at their own 26-yard line and McCarthy returned to the game. The Giants ran the ball to run out the clock on the third quarter.

Facing 3rd-and-5, the Eagles and Giants had offseting penalties. Facing 3rd-and-5 again, the Eagles brought a big blitz but McCarthy got the ball out to Nabers for a first down. Facing 3rd-and-10 after McCarthy threw behind Nabers (good job by Smael Mondon dropping into coverage to force a tougher throw), the Giants QB took off running for a first down into Eagles territory with Andrew Mukuba getting blocked too easily out of making a tackle. The Giants picked up another first down on the ground. Facing 3rd-and-6, Nabers dropped a diving touchdown catch with DeJean trailing that would've sealed the game. Lucky break for the Eagles' defense. The Giants settled for a 38-yard field goal make. 13-play, 54-yard drive to take 6:11 off the clock. EAGLES 8, GIANTS 16.

The Eagles took over at their own 31-yard line. Milton completed a pass to Goedert for 19 yards! Wow! A first down!!! Feel the excitement!!!! Facing 3rd-and-10 after a completion to Elijah Moore went for a three-yard loss (why a designed touch for him in that spot?!), Milton was sacked. Then Mann mishandled the long snap (that was high) and took off running to desperately get a punt off. The Eagles had multiple penalties on the play as well. Lol. Negative two-yard punt!

The Giants took over at the Eagles' 35-yard line with 6:43 left in the game. They ran three times to set up a 49-yard field goal make to go up two possessions. EAGLES 8, GIANTS 19.

The Eagles took over at their own 25-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-8, Milton ran for 24 yards into plus territory. Milton had an interception dropped on a throw where he had Goedert but way underthrew him up the seam. Facing 3rd-and-7, Milton hit Lemon for a first down. Facing 3rd-and-8, Milton hit Elijah Mitchell wide open on the ground and the player stayed on the ground instead of getting up and going beyond the marker. Or at least rolling his way past the sticks?! What the hell?!?! Lol. Especially with that play setting up fourth down after the two-minute warning with time being of the essence. Just not a smart team! The Eagles brought Jake Elliott in for a 45-yard field goal make it bring it to a one-possession game. I would've liked a go there, not the kick. EAGLES 11, GIANTS 19.

The Giants took over at their own 46-yard line with 1:55 on the clock after Elliott's onside kick was not successful for the Eagles. Facing 3rd-and-10 after two runs to force the Eagles to burn timeouts, Singletary ran for two yards to force the Eagles to take their final timeout at 1:42. Punt.

The Eagles took over at their own 5-yard line with 1:32 on the clock and zero timeouts to work with. Milton instantly hit Hollywod Brown for 16 yards with the receiver going out of bounds … until review revealed Brown was in bounds and a 10-second runoff was enforced. Milton tried to take off running but got sacked. Facing 3rd-and-11 after Milton's pass was knocked down at the line of scrimmage, Milton slightly overthrew Cooper on what could've been a touchdown if DC was able to make a one-handed catch. Bayern Munich maintained their unbeaten start to the Bundesliga season with a 2-1 victory away to Mainz 05. Goals from Joshua Kimmich and Lennart Karl put the visitors in control, although a late strike from substitute Philipp Tietz ensured a nervy finish.

The Bavarians ultimately secured all three points to head into the international break on a positive note.

Here is our official match report for the game:

Mainz had a little extra motivation heading into Saturday's clash. Urs Fischer, who made his debut as Mainz coach in last season's 2-2 draw against Bayern, was hoping to cause another upset. After all, the hosts had won four of their previous six home meetings with the record champions - a remarkable record against the Bundesliga giants.

Fischer also had a special message for Nadiem Amiri. Left out of Germany coach Jürgen Klopp's squad for the upcoming Nations League fixtures, the Mainz boss encouraged his star midfielder to use the disappointment as motivation and "show everyone what he's capable of".

Unfortunately for the hosts, Bayern had other plans.

The visitors dominated possession and looked the more dangerous side from the opening minutes. Mainz tried to disrupt their rhythm and create opportunities through set pieces, but Bayern eventually found a way through in the 14th minute.

A misplaced pass in Mainz's build-up handed Harry Kane the opportunity to launch a counterattack. As Sano stepped out to challenge the Englishman, Joshua Kimmich was left completely unmarked in the centre. Ballon d'Or winner Kane picked him out perfectly and the Bayern star made no mistake, smashing the ball underneath the crossbar to put the visitors 1-0 ahead.

Bayern continued to create chances but, much like in recent weeks, struggled to convert several promising opportunities.

Mainz thought they had found their equaliser shortly before the break. Amiri delivered a dangerous free-kick into the box, Jonathan Tah got the slightest touch, and Manuel Neuer missed his attempt to reach the ball. Lee was waiting at the back post and headed it over the line.

However, the celebrations were short-lived. An offside position in the build-up ruled out the goal.

Neuer appeared to pick up an injury during the set-piece incident and was unable to continue. Jonas Urbig replaced the veteran goalkeeper before half-time.

The second half initially offered little in terms of excitement, but Bayern remained firmly in control.

Then came the 57th minute. Konrad Laimer spotted Harry Kane making a run in behind and delivered a superb long ball towards the striker. Kane got his shot away, but after the rebound fell back into his path, he cleverly squared it for Lennart Karl.

The teenager made no mistake, firing home to double Bayern's advantage.

After finding the net against Atlético Madrid in the Champions League, Karl was at it again – this time in Mainz. Not a bad week for the young Bayern sensation!

The goal put Bayern in a comfortable position for the remainder of the match. The visitors appeared to tire somewhat, particularly given their demanding schedule and recent injury concerns.

Bayern appeared to have the game under control in the closing stages, but Mainz made a late attempt to turn things around. Substitute Phillip Tietz pulled one back for the hosts in the 92nd minute, setting up a tense finish. However, the late goal proved insufficient to prevent Bayern from taking all three points.

The victory provides a welcome boost for the visitors ahead of the international break while extending their unbeaten run in the Bundesliga.

Mainz, meanwhile, will have two weeks to regroup and address their recent struggles as they look to get their league campaign back on track.

#2783. Arnav’s Analysis: Takeaways From Rutgers’ 31-10 Loss At Wisconsin

After a first half in which Rutgers hung with Wisconsin, tying the score at 10 before a late Badgers field goal, the Scarlet Knights ran out of steam and did not score once in the second half. It was a stronger performance from AJ Surace, going 14-for-24 for 161 yards and a touchdown of 30 yards to Dyzier Carter, but that was not enough to overcome all the injuries, lack of scoring, and defensive struggles for the Knights.

Defensively, Rutgers held steady for the first half, but the same flaws plagued RU in the second half with wide-open scores, missed tackles, and allowing open throws for the freshman quarterback Ryan Hopkins. Antwan Raymond and Clay Thevenin were held under 100 combined yards despite carrying the football 25 times, and the offense suffered without their top lineman, quarterback, and wide receiver.

Here are my takeaways from another brutal defeat, Rutgers' seventh of this dismal season.

With the Rutgers defense largely holding Wisconsin in check other than the early touchdown, the offense was able to hold serve, and tight end Logan Blake had a nifty catch in triple coverage, having to rip the ball away from Badgers defenders for a first down. Clay Thevenin had three straight carries before Surace found Elias Coke for an 11-yard gain.

After two plays for no gain, Surace found Coke again for a seven-yard pass on third down, and Jack Scullion knocked through a 45-yard field goal to put Rutgers on the board 7-3. The offensive highlight of the day came on the next series, in which three straight run plays led to a beautiful deep ball for Dyzier Carter, who scored his first career touchdown.

However, the second half, the offense completely sputtered, as the opening drive saw a 15-yard pass to Ben Black III and ten yard pass to Dyzier Carter, but resulted in a punt despite getting across midfield. The next couple drives were worse, as the Knights gained eight yards in a three-and-out and then gaining eight net yards with one first down.

With the Badgers cruising down the field for touchdowns, Rutgers did not have the firepower to match any of the scores, and two sacks on Surace led to an incompletion intended for Black on a desparation fourth down heave.

Even a Wisconsin fumble recovered by Rutgers was not enough, as the AJ Surace-led offense was unable to generate any scoring drives or points against the staunch Badgers' front. Cooper Catalano had 14 total tackles and 2.5 per loss, while five different Badgers got home for sacks against a Rutgers offensive line missing star left guard Kwabena Asamoah and right tackle Tyler Needham.

Although at times Antwan Raymond and Clay Thevenin were able to move the ball on the ground, Raymond was limited to 56 yards on 15 carries (3.7 yards per carry), while Thevenin had 10 rushes for 40 yards (four yards per carry). Aiden Gibson and Ja'Shon Benjamin's late carries were negated by yardage lost on sacks by AJ Surace, for a team rushing total of just 94 yards. Surace was briefly replaced by Ashenfelder after an injury saw him leave the field, but he was able to quickly return to the field to finish the drive.

Through the air, Surace was sorely missing KJ Duff, as Black III led the team with six catches for 70 yards. Carter had the lone touchdown and finished with 40 yards on two catches, while Raymond added 21 yards with a reception. Elias Coke and Logan Blake rounded out the receiving column with two catches each for 18 and 14 yards respectively, while Thevenin lost two yards as the receivers were held to 161 total yards.

After both teams exchanged punts on their opening drives, Wisconsin drove down the field with the all too familiar chunk plays through the air: 15-yard pass, 9-yard pass, 18-yard run, and a 21-yard pass from Ryan Hopkins to Eugene Hilton Jr. to take an early 7-0 lead before the Scarlet Knights answered with a field goal.

The defense then held steady, allowing one field goal after a Rutgers three-and-out and punt from their own seven yard line set the Badgers up in plus territory. After the lone Knights' touchdown, they allowed another field goal, spurred by a 26-yard pass to Shamar Rigby and a pass interference on Devonte Anderson.

In the second half, it was an entirely different story, as the Rutgers offense sputtering resulted in repeated scoring drives for Wisconsin. Three separate plays went for 16 yards as the Badgers went up 16-10, then UW made Rutgers pay for a targeting call on Tariq Hayer as Hopkins connected with Ryan Schwendeman over the middle.

The game was largely decided on the next sequence with another Rutgers punt giving way to a 66-yard touchdown pass from Hopkins to tight end Jacob Harris, who ran the ball 47 yards up the right sideline while breaking and evading tackles. Rigby and Harris both crossed 70 yards in four and two plays, respectively.

For the Scarlet Knights, Zaire Angoy had a sack and 1.5 tackles for loss, while Hayer led the team in tackles with seven. Angoy and Kromah combined for a three-yard loss play on Darrion Dupree which set up a field goal, while DJ Allen had Rutgers' other sack.

The rush defense held up relatively well, holding the Badgers' run game to 122 total yards. Hilton led Wisconsin with 39 yards on three carries, while lead back Abu Sama had 35 yards on nine carries. The play of the defensive line has certainly improved, as the Badgers were held to just 4.2 yards per carry.

However, they made a true freshman quarterback making his first start look like a seasoned veteran, as Ryan Hopkins went 18-24 for 241 yards, three touchdowns, and no interceptions. Many of the throws were for over ten yards as the defensive gave up big and intermediate plays in space, as par for the course.

In total, Rutgers allowed 31 points, a near-perfect game from Hopkins, and tons of chunk plays all afternoon as Wisconsin turned a 13-10 halftime lead into a 31-10 victory to clinch bowl eligibility.

Next up for the Scarlet Knights is a Nebraska team that has watched a 5-0 start evaporate into four straight losses. After leading Indiana 17-6, the Cornhuskers fell 20-17 to the Hoosiers, then fell 17-14 at Oregon at the hands of Dylan Raiola and then a stunning defeat to Washington after leading most of the way.

Last week, Nebraska scored the opening touchdown, but the Illini scored three straight, and the Huskers were out of answers after Anthony Colandrea found Jacory Barney Jr. for a long score to cut the lead to eight. It was an upset victory for the Illini, and it sends Nebraska to New Jersey completely reeling.

However, the Scarlet Knights have looked all out of sorts, and are without Asamoah the rest of the season while Duff and Lonergan are uncertain for next week and beyond. Rutgers has never defeated Nebraska despite a few close calls, including the last two meetings which were decided by one point and one touchdown, respectively.

It will be hard to envision Rutgers finding a way to win, with the state of their offense being injured and defense struggling deeply, particularly through the air. However, the month of November continues to get easier, as the Scarlet Knights will have a chance to potentially pick off either Nebraska, Penn State, and Michigan State as the team looks to close out 2026 on a brighter note.
